Tidy Up the Flower Shop review – Repetitive but relaxing

ByKim Snaith 29 October 202629 October 2026
Image: Over the Moon

If I owned a flower shop and opened it up one morning to find that my young niece had “helpfully” unpackaged a huge delivery all over the floor, I’d be furious. Beyond furious, in fact. And yet, that’s exactly the scenario you find yourself facing in Tidy Up the Flower Shop, a cosy organisation game from developer Over the Moon.

Rather than going spare and throttling the kid, however, you simply get on with tidying things up. But it’s no small task. The delivery emptied all over the floor contains over 3,000 individual flowers, all of which must be picked up and put in their rightful place around your store. By using a map on your front desk, you’ll need to locate the correct pots and baskets to place the flowers in and… simply get on with it.

I’ll be honest: when I first loaded up Tidy Up the Flower Shop and saw the scale of the operation ahead of me, I almost noped right out of there. Picking up 3,000-odd flowers, one by one, figuring out where they need to go? It sounds dull as dishwater, and the thought of beginning such a mammoth task felt far too overwhelming.

But then I started doing it… and I found I couldn’t stop. You can hold up to 15 flowers at a time, so I found myself scanning the floors for matching stems, then checking the map to see where in my store they needed to go. After a while, I learned the layout, so I could place flowers without needing to double-check. And if I did happen to put anything in the wrong basket, a handy pop-up would let me know that something wasn’t right, allowing me to quickly rectify my mistake.

Within about 90 minutes, I’d already picked up about half of the flowers on the floor, and seeing my flower shop begin to take shape was a real joy. Yes, Tidy Up the Flower Shop could be considered tedious, and undoubtedly it’s the type of game that many players will find boring. But I find this type of simplistic and repetitious experience seriously relaxing. The only disappointment? I don’t get to keep my flower shop running once it’s been tidied up!

You know exactly what you’re getting with Tidy Up the Flower Shop – the clue is right in the title, after all. It’s not going to be for everyone, but if you’re after a cosy game that offers plenty of tidying and organising, you’re in the right place. Costing just a fiver and offering around four hours of relaxing gameplay, it’s the ideal game to play while listening to a podcast or audiobook.

Tidy Up the Flower Shop Review

You can't really get more simple than Tidy Up the Flower Shop, a game about picking up and correctly putting away more than 3,000 individual flowers. It'll be far too tedious for some players, but if you're the type of person who find repetitive tasks relaxing, it does the job nicely.
7
out of 10

We like…

  • Surprisingly soothing and relaxing
  • Looks and performs well
  • Seeing your flower shop come together is rewarding

We don’t like…

  • Too repetitive for some players

This review of Tidy Up the Flower Shop is based on the PS5 version of the game, with a code provided by the publisher. It’s available on PS5, Xbox Series X/S and PC.
